LESSON: POOL SAFETY HYGIENE

Grade: PP1
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: SWIMMING
Topic 14.1: Pool safety hygiene

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Pool safety hygiene. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Pool safety hygiene means using everyday Kenyan examples
2. describe how Pool safety hygiene appears at home, school, or in the environment
3. practise one safe skill connected to Pool safety hygiene
4. tell why Pool safety hygiene matters for life in Kenya

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: POOL SAFETY HYGIENE
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Pool safety hygiene helps you succeed in PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: POOL SAFETY HYGIENE
Pool safety hygiene is part of Science learning. Connect every idea to something you can observe.
Use safe examples only. Do not try dangerous experiments without a teacher.
Write definitions in your own words, then add one drawing or real-life example.

PART 1: Explain what Pool safety hygiene means using everyday Kenyan examples

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Pool safety hygiene means using everyday Kenyan examples. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Pool safety hygiene means using everyday Kenyan examples.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Pool safety hygiene” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Pool safety hygiene means using everyday Kenyan examples. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe how Pool safety hygiene appears at home, school, or in the environment

What this means
In this part you learn to describe how Pool safety hygiene appears at home, school, or in the environment. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe how Pool safety hygiene appears at home, school, or in the environment.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Pool safety hygiene in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe how Pool safety hygiene appears at home, school, or in the environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise one safe skill connected to Pool safety hygiene

What this means
In this part you learn to practise one safe skill connected to Pool safety hygiene. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise one safe skill connected to Pool safety hygiene.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise one safe skill connected to Pool safety hygiene. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Tell why Pool safety hygiene matters for life in Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to tell why Pool safety hygiene matters for life in Kenya. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: tell why Pool safety hygiene matters for life in Kenya.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Pool safety hygiene” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can tell why Pool safety hygiene matters for life in Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Pool safety hygiene is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Pool safety hygiene” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain what Pool safety hygiene means using everyday Kenyan examples)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Pool safety hygiene in your own words. (skill: describe how Pool safety hygiene appears at home, school, or in the environment)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: practise one safe skill connected to Pool safety hygiene)

Example 4: Show how “Pool safety hygiene” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: tell why Pool safety hygiene matters for life in Kenya)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Pool safety hygiene to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Pool safety hygiene means using everyday Kenyan examples.
3. Practise this skill: describe how Pool safety hygiene appears at home, school, or in the environment.
4. Practise this skill: practise one safe skill connected to Pool safety hygiene.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Pool safety hygiene from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Pool safety hygiene: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Pool safety hygiene?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Pool safety hygiene means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Pool safety hygiene means using everyday Kenyan examples.
5. Be able to: describe how Pool safety hygiene appears at home, school, or in the environment.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
